definitions.meaning: to take fright or grow nervous, a British idiom
to bring up air from the stomach, as a baby does after feeding

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to grow scared, and taken literally it describes bringing gas up from the stomach, which is what a burp does.

clue.text: Look up for instance about hobbles

indicators.note: about puts the turned abbreviation around the word for hobbles
up in a down clue means the abbreviation is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: hobbles means limps

explanation.surface: Searching for an example of someone limping about.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read from bottom to top, so the abbreviation is turned; 'Look' at the start might seem to pair with 'up', but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief look is a quick sight or peek.

definitions.meaning: the moment a plane leaves the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to mimic someone mockingly and the departure of an aircraft into the air.

definitions.meaning: without effort, as of a win
hands on to the next generation, bequeaths

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means winning effortlessly, and literally it means bequeathing or transmitting to heirs.

indicators.note: some say means the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: revolved means spun round, whirled

explanation.surface: Our planet turned on its axis, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: WHIRLED, a word for revolved, is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet is often called simply this, as in around the globe.

indicators.note: misshapen means badly formed, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A deity has been misperceived and is deformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misseen' is an unusual word chosen for its letters; 'misshapen' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is the deity of retribution, punishing hubris.

clue.text: Creature upset about murder and destruction

indicators.note: about puts the turned animal round the word for murder
upset in a down clue means the animal name is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a gnu is an African antelope, a creature
to do in is to murder

explanation.surface: An animal is distressed by a killing and havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the animal over (UNG), since this is a down entry. DO IN is British slang for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin or downfall, the cause of someone's collapse.

indicators.note: indisposed means unwell or out of sorts, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A shepherd who fell ill stayed off work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indisposed' seems to repeat 'Sick', but it is the anagram signal. To SCRIMSHANK is British military slang for shirking duty.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for shirked duty, dodged one's job.

definitions.meaning: the farmyard fowl kept for eggs and meat

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a coward is the same word as the common farmyard fowl.

clue.text: The first man back in sprinted fast

indicators.note: in places the turned name inside the word for sprinted

parts.note: sprinted means ran

indicators.note: back means the name of the first man is read from right to left

parts.note: Adam is the first man in the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the leading runner who dashed back in at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the name to MADA. 'fast' looks like an adverb for the sprinting, but it is the noun: a period of abstaining from food.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim holy month is observed by abstaining from food and drink during daylight, a religious fast.

parts.note: suggests gardening, a layer of fertilizer spread over a flower bed, but means what one wears for sleep

explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nightdresses are what people wear in bed, dressing for the bed.

parts.note: an impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors
a round shape is the letter O
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: Atheist troops are stationed around the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a container indicator but simply gives O. An IMPI is a body of Zulu warriors, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking reverence for God is irreverent or ungodly.

clue.text: Moving with haste and with spirit

definitions.meaning: stylish and lively, full of verve

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both rushing along and having a stylish, spirited flair, as of a gallant hero.

clue.text: Arrows give the lady a fright at first

parts.note: the lady is a woman referred to as she

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word fright is used

explanation.surface: An archer's arrows startle a woman at first sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give' is only a link word. 'at first' takes F from 'fright'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bundle of arrows carried together is called a sheaf, as with a bundle of corn stalks.

definitions.meaning: a failure to notice something, an omission
watchful management or charge of something

explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide' is a link joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an unintended omission and the role of watching over, so it is its own opposite.

clue.text: Call Descartes up about note full of vigour

indicators.note: about puts the reversed phrase around the musical note
up in a down clue means the whole phrase is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness
René Descartes was the French philosopher
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Telephone a philosopher about a lively note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole phrase to ENERETIC, and 'about' wraps that round the note; the French philosopher's first name is René.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively and vigorous, having plenty of drive.

clue.text: A fight about disease and riches

indicators.note: about places the fencing word around the illness word

parts.note: to fence is to fight with swords
flu is a common disease, influenza

explanation.surface: A struggle over an illness and a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes FFLUENCE, which follows the A; 'fight' looks like a noun but works as the verb to fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth and abundance of money, the state of being well-off.

definitions.meaning: a soldier's menial non-military duty, also the uniform worn for it

explanation.definitionFit: The word means tiredness or to tire, and in the army it means menial duties.

clue.text: Divorce? In France, one encounters a snag

parts.note: un is French for one
a hitch is a snag

explanation.surface: Questioning a divorce: in France one hits a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encounters' is a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach or set free, as one untethers a horse, figuratively to separate a couple.

clue.text: Cut short shaggy dog story being told

indicators.note: being told means the phrase is spoken

parts.note: a story about a shaggy dog is a cur tale, a cur being a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone stops a long, rambling joke midway through telling it.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shaggy dog story' is a long joke with a weak punchline, but here it is read literally as a tale about a cur.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten or reduce, to truncate.

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of 'Can yell'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearly, neatly and precisely, without blur.

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting dressed in a boat that is lifted out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' suggests putting on clothes, but it is a sauce or condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomato sauce served on food is a kind of condiment or dressing.

clue.text: Some happy Londoners in the Tower

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Cheerful Londoners are in the Tower of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'in the Tower' does not substitute for the answer: 'in the' is a link and 'Tower' alone defines it. 'the Tower' suggests the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall steel lattice structure carrying power lines is a kind of tower.

clue.text: Chap concealing a weapon in his clothing

indicators.note: concealing means the word for a chap is wrapped around the word for weapon

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a chap
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A man hides a gun inside his coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in his' is only a link; 'concealing' wraps the chap around the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An article of clothing such as a coat or dress is a single item of apparel.

indicators.note: removed says the letters of is are taken away from the drug name

parts.note: digitalis is a heart drug made from foxglove

explanation.surface: A drug is administered by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' takes IS off the end of DIGITALIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The word relates to digits, the fingers, so it describes something done by finger.

clue.text: Learner needs somewhere to drive without precipitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the golf word goes round the weather word

parts.note: a tee is where a golfer drives from
rain is precipitation

explanation.surface: A learner driver needs somewhere to practise when it is not raining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here it means outside, its old sense. 'drive' suggests a car, but it is a golf shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone being taught a job or skill is an apprentice or novice.

clue.text: Without thinking, I chance my all in a flutter

indicators.note: in a flutter means agitated, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gambler bets everything on a whim with a small wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flutter' is British slang for a small bet, so it seems part of the gambling picture; here it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something automatically, like a machine, means acting by rote.
